Living on Credit [6164]

By: Siniketiwe Hlanze | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The rising cost of living is affecting all of us, how far can you stretch the rand?

Unique Selling Point:
Everything is expensive, the recent fuel price hike will see an increase in food costs, NERSA has approved an electricity tariff hike, it's about to be a long and very cold winter in South Africa and consumers are warned to hunker down. But for many, credit like payday loans is the lifeline that will see them through.

Summary:
South Africa's economy is rickety and is susceptible to the turbulence of global economic headwinds, and as economists are warning about stagflation, it's about to get tough for the consumer. A rising cost of living, will only exacerbate the need for credit, in both low and middle income households. With a debt problem that precedes the COVID pandemic, consumers are about to be pulled into a deeper and darker credit whole.

Two loan sharks will give insights into the borrowing trends they observe from their clients; the amount of money they are generally being asked for, the rise in middle class customers needing their help and what the money is generally needed for.

Experts, a case study and vox pops will give the context and create a picture of the current economic environment.

Further information:
Food, fuel and everything is going up. South African consumers are stretched, with salaries barely getting them through to month end, credit has become a lifeline for basic necessities. Households are in a debt chokehold, credit cards, payday loans, revolving loans are keeping consumers afloat. This cycle leaves many vulnerable to high interest unsecured loans, with no savings for emergencies, these loans are both a reprieve and can sink a person's finances. The NCR Credit Bureau Monitor says out of the 24.4 million credit active consumers, 10.17 million have impaired records. These are people that are struggling to meet their monthly credit debit orders and obligations. With impaired records, they can no longer access credit from banks, they turn to mashonisas. The unregulated loan sharks, known for high interest loans and a history of using the most unscrupulous means of collecting their money. Legally, the highest interest that can be charged on credit is 30 percent, however loan sharks are known to charge up to 40 percent. For a desperate consumer, the interest is often something they'll overlook till it's time to pay back the money.

Script:


Claire
Monthly basics have become expensive, consumer spending is tame and salaries are shrinking in the face of rising inflation.


We’re using credit cards for monthly necessities, like groceries, it’s a crutch for many households.

Families are supplementing their income with loans, credit cards and overdrafts. It’s a monthly cycle that doesn’t end, sinking many homes into debt Simphiwe

Oh my goodness we had credit cards and accounts, clothing accounts, yes we used to buy our food on credit.
Claire
Youtuber and content creator, Simphiwe Ntuli built her middle class lifestyle on credit.

Newly married and renting an apartment in the suburbs, she was a student and her husband worked full time.
They were moving up in life.

A call offering him vehicle finance came at the right time, a new car seemed a perfect purchase.

Simphiwe
He told me that look, they say I qualify for this but then in my range I also qualify for this. And then I was like why would you go small when you can go big.
Claire
At what point did you start realising, we actually can’t afford this luxury car that we’ve bought?

Simphiwe
When we couldn’t even maintain our own monthly lifestyle that we used to live on. We liked eating out, that became a struggle, buying groceries at the shopping mall, we’d just get basics. I can’t have guests over anymore cause there’s nothing in the cupboards.

Claire
Living beyond their means and an additional debit order for a car they couldn’t afford. The young couple was now struggling to make ends meet.


In trying to undo the financial damage and ease their stress, her husband took the car back to the dealership.

Simphiwe
I was at school one day, and he took the car back. I lost my mind. I couldn’t believe it, I went to the parking lot like seven times to check that the car is literally gone. That was the first time he slept actually, that day
But there were still outstanding payments and now with a baby on the way, something had to give.

Simphiwe
So we literally had to move back home to a backroom, at his parents house.
Simphiwe and her husband were drowning in debt, desperation pushed them to loan sharks also knowns as mashonisa, to borrow money to see them through the month.
Mchunu
Sometimes you earn R10 000 but your costs they are R150 00, so you need to balance the figure, so that’s when you come to me.
This man is one of Soweto’s infamous loan sharks, we’re not using his full name for legal reasons.

Mchunu, is shrewd and sharp, he counts professionals and businessmen as his clients.

Mchunu.
They are desperate, some it’s a norm now to them. Which is my regular client. So a person like that is helping me to run the business and I’m helping them to move forward.
Claire
It’s an unregulated and unregistered business, it’s not known how many people have found themselves trapped in the jaws of a loan shark.

However, with over 700 000 South Africans currently under debt review, it’s an indication that consumers are regularly skipping payments on their bills and many lives are built on credit.

Claire
Neil Roets is the founder of Debt Rescue, he helps create a financial life line for clients drowning in debt
Claire
Salaries are paying off debt leaving households with little to see them through the month.

Neil
Even before COVID almost half of all credit active consumers were over indebted, meaning that they were arrears of three months in at least one of their accounts.


South Africa’s borrowing culture continues to grow, even supermarkets are selling groceries on credit.

David Obrien is the Managing Director at Meerkat, a debt counseling firm in Cape Town.

David Obrien
a desperate consumer will take those credit initially, maybe because it's easy.

But ultimately that debt builds up. And if you're not setting your debt, then then you're effectively paying an extra 28% interest on your bananas. And that's not good.

That’s easily R10 extra on a kilogram of bananas.
CALL CENTRE MONTAGE

Abdullah Laher knows these statistics only too well. He runs MRT Collections, each agent at his debt collecting firm makes on average 80 phone calls per day tracking down consumers in arrears on their bills.
Abdulla

People tend to postpone the call, call me back later, call me tonight.
Claire
what type of debts are we chasing here
Abdullah
Retail, home loans, vehicle finance, municipal accounts are growing day by day
Abdullah
We’re not here to harass you, we’re here to assist you. We’re trying to assist you with that loans where you’re getting charged every single month interest, where you’re getting charged every single call we make, you’re getting charged for smses, you’re getting charged for letters that we’re sending you on a monthly basis.

Tsungai Masendeke is a financial planner with a clientele in Joburg’s northern suburbs.

Claire
Meaning loans for houses and cars are cheaper in monthly interest rate fees.

Tsungai
So if you do not have an asset backing your loan the interest rate are going to be high. Which is why your store loans are probably the most expensive. YOU’LL find that your personal loans equally expensive, your credit cards are expensive but your motor vehicle loans and your mortgages are going to be cheapest debt you could ever have.
So I find individuals who say I want to kill off my bond, no honey start, with the personal loan, cause that’s what costing you the most on a month to month basis.

Claire
But not even valuable financial advice is enough to rescue some people from their debt spiral.

LINK
This year’s interest rates hikes have been biting..
Whilst the formal sector’s interests costs are regulated, unregistered lenders, like loan sharks have carte blanche on the interest they charge you.
Over the years Mchunu has devised his own affordability scale.

Small loans are repaid at 30 percent interest rate, but amounts over R10 000 return with 50 percent interest.

Mchunu
50 percent is steep I know but we check, I check first, that how much do you earn. And what are your responsibilities? So that I don’t kill you in this 50 percent.
I do my own researches. That if I borrow a nurse or I borrow a teacher, if I’m gonna put that percentage, how much is that person earning. 04;38 you mustn’t over charge cause you need customers, 04:58 because they need you, you need them.

Claire
Desperate clients, like Simphiwe, overlook the exorbitant interest and the shameless tactics when they need cash.
For Mchunu, it’s a necessary evil, holding onto client I.Ds and sometimes appliances as collateral, in case he doesn’t get his money back.

Mchunu
Like, I take your things if you are a first client. Cause I don’t have any reference with you and I have any mutual trust. 12;35 because they can be a flight risk
But things that I’ve took like fridges, stoves, eh a bowser eh it’s a lot, I must take out my shoes even to count with my toes.
It’s unscrupulous and illegal.


Neil
That unfortunately just makes everything worse because what the national credit act also ensures that credit providers does not give out reckless loans, reckless credit so they must make sure that people can afford to pay back those loans. But unfortunately that’s not always the case with loan sharks
And with the country’s economic forecast looking gloomy, experts are warning consumers to save for a rainy day, to cushion against looming hard times and being vulnerable to cunning loan sharks


David Obrien
We're going to face inflation for the next couple of years. People should start tightening their belts now, trying to create some some free air between what they earn and what they spend every month and maybe take that little extra and put it away in an emergency savings fund.


Claire
Assessing your bank statement and budgeting is a moment of reckoning with your spending habits.
Financial advisors say it’s the first step to getting ourselves out of money troubles.

Tsungai
It is the best advise outside of eating your vegetables. A budget is a money management exercise that helps you to ascertain how much is coming in and how much is leaving and when you can monitor and when you can track, you can then manage it much better.

Claire
So where are you now, with your husband in terms of your financial health.
Simphiwe
After paying the debts and then we stopped going to mashonisa, Car we drive, yabona mabathi you afford for this one, we want the one underneath that one. That’s what we drive now and we are happy.
Claire
It's a priceless feeling, debt free at a time when many families are getting by on credit
